Let $\Omega$ be a measure space whose measure $\mathbb P$ is a probability measure, and let $X_1, X_2, 	ilde X_1, 	ilde X_2 : \Omega 	o G$ be measurable functions. Notation: for a measure space $\Omega$ with measure $\mu$ and a random variable $Z:\Omega	o S$, $H[Z]$ denotes the entropy of $Z$, i.e. the entropy of the law (pushforward measure) $Z_*\mu$; $H[Z\mid W\leftarrow w]$ denotes the entropy of $Z$ conditioned on the event $W=w$. For $G$-valued random variables $U$ on $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $V$ on $(\Omega',\mu')$, the Ruzsa distance is $d[U;V]:=H_{
u}[(x,y)\mapsto x-y]-	frac12H[U]-	frac12H[V]$, where $H_
u[(x,y)\mapsto x-y]$ is the entropy of the map $(x,y)\mapsto x-y$ on $G	imes G$ under the product $
u=U_*\mu\otimes V_*\mu'$ of the two laws (equivalently, $H[U'-V']-H[U']/2-H[V']/2$ for independent copies $U',V'$ of $U,V$). (Each random variable is taken with respect to the measure of its own space: $\mathbb P_{01}$, $\mathbb P_{02}$ or $\mathbb P$.) For random variables $Y_1:\Omega_1	o G$, $Y_2:\Omega_2	o G$ on spaces with measures $\mu_1,\mu_2$, define $	au[Y_1;Y_2]:=d[Y_1;Y_2]+\eta\,d[X^0_1;Y_1]+\eta\,d[X^0_2;Y_2]$. Assume that $(X_1,X_2)$ minimizes $	au$ in the sense that for all probability measures $
u_1,
